input: Scheduled ventures brief: develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue-generating software; merge when done.
task: hvac-load-calc: basements below grade and skylights

errors.what: First browser check read results with innerText, which skips hidden sections, so it reported the new rows as missing.
errors.fix: Reran with textContent: all three new outputs are present.

errors.what: The draft README/post first gave the FD comparison from 5 of 7 rows (the table was still running) and said the floor loss 'rises by three quarters'.
errors.fix: Rewrote both from the full table: wall 10-16% low bare, within 5% insulated; floor 5-43% low; +28% floor rise.

integrity_issues.what: I wanted to cite published below-grade U tables for the check, but the source (WAC 51-11C Table A104.1) was unreachable through the proxy and the values I remembered could not be verified.
integrity_issues.fix: No unverified table is cited. The closed forms are checked against an independent 2-D finite-volume soil solve written for this run instead.

doc_friction.issue: Start here sent two sessions to the same open-tennis-robots item within 2 seconds (#17513 and #17514); claim_check caught it, but only after both claims were pushed.

open-tennis-robots' buildable item is a chain of pre-registered take-grid tests on simulated data (nine-point, eight-point, then the 1 ms point). Each step changes very little; the row could say so, so runs can weigh it.

deviations.why: Yielded the routed flagship row after the claim race and did not take the next flagship rows: all were worked several times a day by other sessions, with open PRs. I deepened a non-flagship construction/energy venture (hvac-load-calc) in the owner's industrial/energy/construction direction instead, filling two gaps its own docs listed (basements, skylights).
deviations.did: Added below-grade wall and floor loss with an independent 2-D soil check, plus skylights, page inputs, docs and a post.
deviations.result: Merged with 65 of 65 tests passing; the check found the floor closed form 5-43% low, which is now stated on the page.

goal: Deepen a construction/energy tool: a house load calculator that handles basements and skylights
notes: Verification: run_venture_tests.py hvac-load-calc: ok, 65 tests. Headless Chromium: the page with a basement room and a skylight shows 'Basement walls below grade', 'Skylights (sun)' and the ground temperature, with no console errors. FD grid check (24x7 ft bare wall): 0.1957/0.1962/0.1958 at 0.5/0.25/0.125 ft. Preflight output is in the PR thread if it finished before the merge.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: an HVAC engineer adding below-grade and skylight loads, writing a 2-D conduction check and tests

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
